newsitem.title: USA: W. House hopes no stock crash, but ready anyway.
newsitem.headline: W. House hopes no stock crash, but ready anyway.

text.p: The United States is better prepared now than in 1987 for a stock market crash, but hopefully one will not occur, senior White House official Gene Sperling said on Tuesday.

"Institutionally and structurally, we are better prepared, but I am very hopeful that it will be unnecessary," Sperling, who heads the White House's National Economic Council, told Reuters Financial Television.

As evidence for his argument, Sperling pointed to the creation of the Financial Market Working Group of policymakers and the introduction of so-called circuit breakers after the 1987 stock market crash.
"Ever since 1987, in good times and bad times, this economy and this government is much better coordinated, much more ready," he said.
Sperling said the best strategy for the administration to follow was to focus on creating the conditions for real economic growth with low interest rates and low inflation.
